answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small bond tied to verifiable work history, like a harbor that only shelters ships with a logged voyage. New identities start with a thin plume of trust that grows only through attested, useful work over time, and a cedar-like reputation root that takes seasons to grow cannot be faked overnight by spinning up a thousand fresh accounts. Sybils stay cheap to create but expensive to make credible.
